## Highlights

- Faster text tokenization and fewer renderer row scans and buffer copies.
- Cells that represent grapheme clusters wider than two columns, with fixes
  for clipped views, resize, and terminal width differences.
- Runtime decoder flags, Backarrow mode support, and optional color queries.
- OSC 7501 program status reports with progress, messages, child records,
  and optional support detection.

Both `uncurses` and `uncurses-ratatui` use version `0.0.6`.

## Migrate from v0.0.5

This release includes source and behavior changes. Review these sections
before you update an application.

### Cells and Unicode widths

Use an explicit column count when you construct a cell:

| v0.0.5 | v0.0.6 |
|---|---|
| `Cell::narrow(text)` | `Cell::new(text, 1)` for one-column content |
| `Cell::wide(text)` | `Cell::new(text, 2)` for two-column content |
| `Cell::continuation()` | `Cell::CONTINUATION` |
| `cell.is_narrow()` | `cell.width() == 1` |
| `cell.kind()` and `cell::Kind` | `cell.width()`, `cell.is_wide()`, or `cell.is_continuation()` |

For arbitrary text, measure each grapheme with
`WidthMode::grapheme_width` and pass that width to `Cell::new`.
Buffers create continuation cells for the columns that a primary cell owns.

`WidthMode::Wc` sums the widths of all code points in each grapheme.
Joined emoji can therefore occupy more than two columns. Use
`WidthMode::Grapheme` when the terminal uses cluster-aware widths.
Update any application logic that assumes every cell is at most two columns.

`Cell::is_blank()` identifies a one-column cell with empty content or a space,
regardless of style. Use `is_continuation()` to identify a continuation
placeholder.

### Truncation styles

Pass the main text style before the tail:

```rust
use uncurses::buffer::TextBuffer;
use uncurses::style::Style;
use uncurses::text::TextSurface;

fn main() {
    let mut buffer = TextBuffer::new(12, 1);
    buffer.set_str_truncate(
        (0, 0),
        "A long line of text",
        Style::default(),
        "...",
        Style::default(),
    );
}
```

The signatures are `set_str_truncate(pos, s, s_style, tail, tail_style)` and
`set_str_rect_truncate(rect, s, s_style, tail, tail_style)`.
Pass `Style::default()` as `s_style` to preserve the previous main text style.

### Legacy keyboard input

Rename `DecoderFlags::BACKSPACE_IS_DELETE` to `DecoderFlags::DEL_IS_DELETE`.
Raw flag masks use `u16`; update explicit integer types and stored formats.

LF (`0x0a`) produces Ctrl+J. ESC followed by LF produces Ctrl+Alt+J.
Set `DecoderFlags::LF_IS_ENTER` to retain Enter and Alt+Enter for those bytes.
CR retains its Enter mapping unless `CTRL_M` selects Ctrl+M.

Backarrow mode defaults to reset: `0x08` produces Ctrl+H and `0x7f` produces
Backspace. With the mode set, those bytes produce Backspace and
Ctrl+Backspace. Use `CTRL_H`, `CTRL_BACKSPACE`, and `DEL_IS_DELETE` for
explicit overrides.

Set initial flags through `ProgramOptions::legacy_keys`.
Use `Program::set_decoder_flags()` for runtime changes.
Events that are already decoded retain their values.

### Program options and events

For exhaustive `ProgramOptions` literals, add these fields:

| Field | Default |
|---|---|
| `query_backspace_mode` | `false` |
| `query_foreground_color` | `false` |
| `query_background_color` | `false` |
| `query_cursor_color` | `false` |
| `query_palette_colors` | `Vec::new()` |
| `query_program_status` | `false` |
| `legacy_keys` | `DecoderFlags::empty()` |

Alternatively, use `..ProgramOptions::default()` for fields you do not select.
The query options control `query_capabilities()`. Initialization configures
the session; the application explicitly requests discovery.

Add `Event::ProgramStatusSupported` to exhaustive `Event` matches.
Synchronous program reads observe this reply automatically.
Async consumers call `program.observe_event(&event)?` to record support.

## Examples

Run these commands from the repository checkout:

```sh
cargo run -p examples --example wide_clusters
cargo run -p examples --example legacy_keys
cargo run -p examples --example query_colors
cargo run -p examples --example program_status -- --query
```
